raw_response:
I will keep things simple and steady this year. I am 76, so I do not want to spread myself across too many crops or take big risks. In Quzhou, the wheat and summer maize rotation is what I know best, and it fits the land, the weather, and the way I can still manage the work. So I will use the same land for winter wheat first, then follow with summer maize after the wheat harvest. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is reliable and easier for me to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is usually better. I will not plant labor-heavy cash crops this year. I want a plan that is familiar, stable, and not too hard on my body.

For wheat, I will focus on getting an even stand, enough base fertilizer, and timely water at the key stages. I will plough before sowing to make the soil loose and let the roots go down well. I will give nitrogen the most, with moderate phosphorus and potassium, because wheat here responds clearly to that. I will irrigate about three times if water is available, mainly at overwintering recovery, jointing, and grain filling. I will spray a couple of times if I see disease, aphids, or too many weeds, but I will not spray more than needed. After wheat harvest, I will move straight into summer maize on the same land. To save labor and catch soil moisture, I will use no-tillage sowing for maize. I will still fertilize it properly, with nitrogen as the main nutrient, and I will water about twice if the rain is not enough. I will keep pesticide use moderate and only use it when pressure is real. My goal is not the highest possible yield. My goal is a steady harvest that I can manage safely and on time.
